forecast.ci_interpretation: ci95_low/ci95_high is a 95% Wilson score interval for the share of simulated tournaments won. It measures only the random error from using a finite number of simulations (it shrinks as n_sims grows). It does NOT include uncertainty about the match model, the ratings, or the unplayed draw, so the true forecast uncertainty is larger.
assumptions: Ratings and form are frozen at the prediction cutoff and are not updated during a simulated tournament.
Scores are independent Poisson draws; extra time uses one third of the 90-minute rates; shoot-outs are a coin flip.
League-phase ties still level after the opponent-based criteria are broken at random (disciplinary record and club coefficient are not available).
The knockout draw is sampled uniformly from all outcomes consistent with the pairings already known; no other draw restrictions are modelled.
Monte Carlo intervals measure simulation noise only, not uncertainty in the match model.

selection_notes: Selection basis: horizon-matched (frozen-state) rolling-origin folds for seasons <= 2022/23, 869 matches. The simulator freezes team state at the cutoff, so models are compared in exactly that setting; the test seasons were not used to choose.
With 869 selection matches, ['logistic_elo', 'poisson_elo', 'poisson', 'logistic'] cannot be statistically distinguished from 'elo' (difference within one standard error).
caveats: train=1244, validation=250, test=314 matches. A multiclass log-loss standard error on a few hundred matches is roughly 0.03-0.04, so model differences smaller than that are within noise.
The test period has fewer than 500 matches: treat its metrics as a rough health check, not a precise ranking of models.
Calibration bins hold only a few dozen matches each; reliability curves are indicative only.
